On 2023-02-28, the user asked what documents are needed to start developing a game, then asked how to make a Game Design Document (GDD) and a Technical Design Document (TDD).

Guidance given to the user described typical game-development documents as a Game Design Document (GDD) covering the game's concept, mechanics, and vision; a Technical Design Document (TDD) covering technical specifications, requirements, and architecture; a project plan with schedule, milestones, and budget; contracts or agreements for collaborators; and intellectual-property documentation such as trademark/copyright registrations or NDAs. Needs vary by project scope and complexity.

Guidance given to the user for making a Game Design Document (GDD) recommended describing the concept, genre, target audience, and distinctive appeal; outlining rules, objectives, controls, and core mechanics; documenting story, characters, setting, and lore; specifying visual style and user interface; listing technical requirements; planning timeline, milestones, budget, team, and resources; and adding supporting materials such as references, concept art, and prototypes. The GDD should be clear but adaptable and updated as the game evolves.

Guidance given to the user for making a Technical Design Document (TDD) recommended defining scope and technical requirements; specifying hardware, software, and dependencies; diagramming game architecture and system interactions; documenting data structures and algorithms; setting performance targets such as frame rate and load times; planning debugging and testing; and explaining build, test, deployment, and post-release maintenance processes. The TDD should be comprehensive but adaptable and updated during development.

The assistant explained that NPs generally have graduate-level nursing education and additional clinical training, and may diagnose and treat illnesses, prescribe medication, order and interpret tests, and manage patient care. The assistant cited U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics median annual wages from May 2020: $117,670 for nurse practitioners and $75,330 for registered nurses. It said pay varies with experience, location, and specialization.

The assistant described NP career paths including advanced practice and leadership, independent practice, hospitals and emergency rooms, specialties such as family practice, pediatrics, geriatrics, and psychiatry, management, research, and academia. RN advancement may include charge-nurse or other leadership roles and specialties such as emergency, critical care, and pediatrics; further education can enable RNs to pursue other paths.

The assistant cited historical U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projections for 2019–2029: NP employment growth of 45% and RN employment growth of 7%. The assistant identified primary care in underserved or rural areas, specialty care including cardiology, neurology, and oncology, urgent care and emergency medicine, and psychiatric or mental health care as areas of NP demand.
